requirements.quote: The payload of the CONNECT Packet contains one or more length-prefixed fields, whose presence is determined by the flags in the variable header. These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password [MQTT-3.1.3-1].
requirements.condition: For every CONNECT packet payload
requirements.required_behavior: Include at least one payload field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A CONNECT payload with zero fields is not permitted.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed payload field count can be checked against the lower bound of one.

requirements.quote: The payload of the CONNECT Packet contains one or more length-prefixed fields, whose presence is determined by the flags in the variable header. These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password [MQTT-3.1.3-1].
requirements.condition: For every field contained in a CONNECT payload
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the field with a length prefix.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode an unframed payload field.
requirements.why_checkable: Each payload field can be parsed for its leading length and bounded data.

requirements.quote: The payload of the CONNECT Packet contains one or more length-prefixed fields, whose presence is determined by the flags in the variable header. These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password [MQTT-3.1.3-1].
requirements.condition: When deciding which optional fields appear in a CONNECT payload
requirements.required_behavior: Make field presence consistent with the flags in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include or omit a conditional field contrary to its controlling flag.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser can compare each variable-header flag with the corresponding payload-field presence.

requirements.quote: The payload of the CONNECT Packet contains one or more length-prefixed fields, whose presence is determined by the flags in the variable header. These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password [MQTT-3.1.3-1].
requirements.condition: When CONNECT payload fields are present
requirements.required_behavior: Order them as Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password, omitting only fields whose flags make them absent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place any present field out of the listed relative order.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed field sequence can be compared directly with the ordered subsequence of the listed fields.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (ClientId) identifies the Client to the Server. Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId. The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server [MQTT-3.1.3-2].
requirements.condition: For Clients concurrently connecting to a Server
requirements.required_behavior: Use a unique ClientId for each Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Two connected Clients must not share the same effective ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: The Server's active connection table can be checked for duplicate effective ClientIds.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (ClientId) identifies the Client to the Server. Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId. The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server [MQTT-3.1.3-2].
requirements.condition: When a Client identifies state held for an MQTT Session with a Server
requirements.required_behavior: Use the ClientId as the session-state identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify that session state without the ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: Client persistence and reconnect behavior can be correlated with the ClientId used for the session.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (ClientId) identifies the Client to the Server. Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId. The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server [MQTT-3.1.3-2].
requirements.condition: When a Server identifies state held for an MQTT Session with a Client
requirements.required_behavior: Use the ClientId as the session-state identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify that session state without the ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: Server session-state lookup can be exercised with distinct and repeated ClientIds.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (ClientId) MUST be present and MUST be the first field in the CONNECT packet payload [MQTT-3.1.3-3].
requirements.condition: For every CONNECT packet payload
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Client Identifier field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A CONNECT payload without ClientId is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed and checked for ClientId presence.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (ClientId) MUST be present and MUST be the first field in the CONNECT packet payload [MQTT-3.1.3-3].
requirements.condition: For every CONNECT packet payload
requirements.required_behavior: Place ClientId as the first field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place another payload field before ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: The first parsed payload field can be checked for the ClientId type.

requirements.quote: The ClientId MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.1.3-4].
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Represent ClientId as an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode ClientId using another string or binary representation.
requirements.why_checkable: The length-prefixed bytes can be validated with the MQTT UTF-8 string rules.

requirements.quote:
The Server MUST allow ClientIds which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters
"0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" [MQTT-3.1.3-5].
requirements.condition: When a ClientId is 1 through 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes long and every character is in the listed alphanumeric set
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must accept the ClientId with respect to its length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject such a ClientId because its encoded length is anywhere in the inclusive 1..23 range.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary and interior lengths using listed characters can be submitted and the Server's acceptance observed.

requirements.quote:
The Server MUST allow ClientIds which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters
"0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" [MQTT-3.1.3-5].
requirements.condition: When a ClientId is 1 through 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes long and consists only of characters from 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must accept the ClientId with respect to its character content.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject such a ClientId because it uses any character in the listed set.
requirements.why_checkable: ClientIds covering every listed character can be submitted within the mandatory length range.

requirements.quote: The Server MAY allow ClientId’s that contain more than 23 encoded bytes. The Server MAY allow ClientId’s that contain characters not included in the list given above.
requirements.condition: When a ClientId is more than 23 encoded bytes long
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to accept it.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes this extension optional and imposes no mandatory acceptance or rejection outcome.

requirements.quote: The Server MAY allow ClientId’s that contain more than 23 encoded bytes. The Server MAY allow ClientId’s that contain characters not included in the list given above.
requirements.condition: When a ClientId contains a character outside the mandatory alphanumeric set
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to accept it.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes this extension optional and imposes no mandatory acceptance or rejection outcome.

requirements.quote: A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientId that has a length of zero bytes, however if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientId to that Client. It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientId [MQTT-3.1.3-6].
requirements.condition: When a Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to accept it.
requirements.why_checkable: The acceptance choice is optional, so the permission itself supplies no required observable outcome.

requirements.quote: A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientId that has a length of zero bytes, however if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientId to that Client. It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientId [MQTT-3.1.3-6].
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts a zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a unique ClientId to that Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue using the zero-byte value or an identifier already assigned to another Client.
requirements.why_checkable: The effective identifiers of multiple zero-ID connections can be inspected for nonempty uniqueness.

requirements.quote: A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientId that has a length of zero bytes, however if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientId to that Client. It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientId [MQTT-3.1.3-6].
requirements.condition: After the Server assigns a unique ClientId for an accepted zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Process the CONNECT packet as though the Client had supplied the assigned ClientId.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process session identity using the original zero-byte value.
requirements.why_checkable: Session creation and subsequent identity-dependent behavior can be compared with an explicit-ID connection.

requirements.quote: If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId, the Client MUST also set CleanSession to 1 [MQTT-3.1.3-7].
requirements.condition: When the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Set CleanSession to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The combination zero-byte ClientId and CleanSession=0 is forbidden for a Client.
requirements.why_checkable: The ClientId length and CleanSession bit can be checked in one CONNECT packet.

requirements.quote: If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection [MQTT-3.1.3-8].
requirements.condition: When the Server receives zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession=0
requirements.required_behavior: Send CONNACK with return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not return a success code or a different rejection code.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed CONNECT can be injected and the exact CONNACK return byte observed.

requirements.quote: If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection [MQTT-3.1.3-8].
requirements.condition: After sending the required 0x02 CONNACK for zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession=0
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after the CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet/connection trace can verify both closure and its ordering after CONNACK.

requirements.quote: If the Server rejects the ClientId it MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection [MQTT-3.1.3-9].
requirements.condition: When the Server rejects a ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Send CONNACK with return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not return a success code or a different rejection code.
requirements.why_checkable: A rejected identifier can be submitted and the exact CONNACK return byte observed.

requirements.quote: If the Server rejects the ClientId it MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection [MQTT-3.1.3-9].
requirements.condition: After sending the required 0x02 CONNACK for a rejected ClientId
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after the CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet/connection trace can verify both closure and its ordering after CONNACK.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will Topic is the next field in the payload. The Will Topic MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.1.3-10].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Place Will Topic as the payload field immediately following ClientId.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place another conditional field between ClientId and Will Topic.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed CONNECT payload sequence can be inspected at the field following ClientId.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will Topic is the next field in the payload. The Will Topic MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.1.3-10].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Will Topic as an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode Will Topic as arbitrary binary data or another string representation.
requirements.why_checkable: The length-prefixed Will Topic bytes can be validated against the MQTT UTF-8 rules.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Place Will Message as the payload field immediately following Will Topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place User Name or Password before Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed CONNECT payload sequence can be checked at the field following Will Topic.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: When the stored Will is published
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will Message field as the Application Message published to Will Topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish unrelated application data as the Will.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT Will Message bytes can be compared with the later Will publication.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: When encoding the Will Message field
requirements.required_behavior: Prefix its data with a two-byte length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a length prefix of another width.
requirements.why_checkable: The two leading bytes and subsequent field boundary are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: Within the Will Message field
requirements.required_behavior: Place the Will payload bytes immediately after the two-byte length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place unrelated bytes between the length and data.
requirements.why_checkable: The field layout can be parsed from the first two bytes into the following data region.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: For the Will Message data portion
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the payload as a sequence of bytes and permit zero-length data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require at least one Will Message data byte.
requirements.why_checkable: A two-byte zero length with no following data is a directly constructible boundary case.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding Will Message length
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the data length in the inclusive range 0 through 65535 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode more data than a two-byte length can represent.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-byte length and explicit zero-length allowance give a testable 0..65535 byte domain.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: When computing the Will Message length value
requirements.required_behavior: Set it equal to the number of data bytes that follow.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a length that differs from the following data byte count.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared length can be compared with the actual following data count.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 the Will Message is the next field in the payload. The Will Message defines the Application Message that is to be published to the Will Topic as described in Section 3.1.2.5. This field consists of a two byte length followed by the payload for the Will Message expressed as a sequence of zero or more bytes. The length gives the number of bytes in the data that follows and does not include the 2 bytes taken up by the length itself.
requirements.condition: When computing the Will Message length value
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude the two length-prefix bytes themselves.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not add 2 for the prefix width.
requirements.why_checkable: The prefix width and following data count can be measured independently.

requirements.quote: When the Will Message is published to the Will Topic its payload consists only of the data portion of this field, not the first two length bytes.
requirements.condition: When publishing the Will Message to Will Topic
requirements.required_behavior: Use only the data portion as the Application Message payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the two Will Message length bytes in the published payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT field bytes and emitted PUBLISH payload can be compared byte for byte.

requirements.quote: If the User Name Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The User Name MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.1.3-11]. It can be used by the Server for authentication and authorization.
requirements.condition: When the User Name Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Place User Name as the next payload field after all preceding present fields.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place Password before User Name.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed payload sequence can be compared with the controlling flags and required order.

requirements.quote: If the User Name Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The User Name MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.1.3-11]. It can be used by the Server for authentication and authorization.
requirements.condition: When the User Name Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Encode User Name as an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode User Name as arbitrary binary data or another string representation.
requirements.why_checkable: The length-prefixed bytes can be validated against the MQTT UTF-8 string rules.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).
requirements.condition: When the Password Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Place Password as the next field in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not parse the Password data at a position other than the next field selected by the payload flags.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed payload sequence can be checked for Password after the other flag-selected fields.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).
requirements.condition: For the Password field data
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the contents as binary data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require Password data to satisfy UTF-8 string rules.
requirements.why_checkable: Arbitrary octet values can be submitted and compared with the parsed Password bytes.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).
requirements.condition: For the Password field data length
requirements.required_behavior: Allow values from 0 through 65535 bytes inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode more than 65535 Password data bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary payloads at 0 and 65535 bytes can be serialized and parsed.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).
requirements.condition: When encoding Password
requirements.required_behavior: Prefix the binary data with a two-byte length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a length prefix of another width.
requirements.why_checkable: The Password field prefix width is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).
requirements.condition: When computing the Password length value
requirements.required_behavior: Set it equal to the number of Password binary-data bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a length that differs from the binary-data byte count.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared value can be compared with the actual data length.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, this is the next field in the payload. The Password field contains 0 to 65535 bytes of binary data prefixed with a two byte length field which indicates the number of bytes used by the binary data (it does not include the two bytes taken up by the length field itself).
requirements.condition: When computing the Password length value
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude the two length-field bytes themselves.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not add the prefix width to the data length.
requirements.why_checkable: The prefix width and data byte count can be measured independently.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.7 - Password bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	Data length MSB
byte 2	Data length LSB
byte 3 ….	Data, if length > 0.
requirements.condition: Within the Password field
requirements.required_behavior: Put the most significant length byte at byte 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not put the least significant length byte at byte 1.
requirements.why_checkable: Password-field byte 1 can be compared with the high eight bits of the length.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.7 - Password bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	Data length MSB
byte 2	Data length LSB
byte 3 ….	Data, if length > 0.
requirements.condition: Within the Password field
requirements.required_behavior: Put the least significant length byte at byte 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not put the most significant length byte at byte 2.
requirements.why_checkable: Password-field byte 2 can be compared with the low eight bits of the length.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.7 - Password bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	Data length MSB
byte 2	Data length LSB
byte 3 ….	Data, if length > 0.
requirements.condition: When Password data length is greater than 0
requirements.required_behavior: Start the binary data at byte 3 of the Password field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not start data before or after byte 3.
requirements.why_checkable: The first data octet offset can be checked after the two-byte length prefix.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.7 - Password bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	Data length MSB
byte 2	Data length LSB
byte 3 ….	Data, if length > 0.
requirements.condition: When encoding the two-byte Password length
requirements.required_behavior: Use most-significant-byte-first order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the length in little-endian order.
requirements.why_checkable: The consecutive MSB then LSB rows establish a directly testable big-endian representation.

requirements.quote: Note that a Server MAY support multiple protocols (including earlier versions of this protocol) on the same TCP port or other network endpoint. If the Server determines that the protocol is MQTT 3.1.1 then it validates the connection attempt as follows.
requirements.condition: At a TCP port or other network endpoint used for MQTT
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to support additional protocols, including earlier MQTT versions.
requirements.why_checkable: This permission does not require multi-protocol support and therefore supplies no mandatory observable outcome.

requirements.quote: 1.If the Server does not receive a CONNECT Packet within a reasonable amount of time after the Network Connection is established, the Server SHOULD close the connection.
requirements.condition: When no CONNECT arrives within a reasonable time after establishing the Network Connection
requirements.error_behavior: The Server should close the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The phrase “reasonable amount of time” does not define a measurable deadline, so the condition is incomplete for deterministic testing.

requirements.quote: 2.The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT Packet conforms to section 3.1 and close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK if it does not conform [MQTT-3.1.4-1].
requirements.condition: When the Server receives a CONNECT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Validate the packet against all requirements of section 3.1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept a CONNECT packet that fails section 3.1 validation.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed CONNECT variants can be injected and their acceptance or rejection observed.

requirements.quote: 2.The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT Packet conforms to section 3.1 and close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK if it does not conform [MQTT-3.1.4-1].
requirements.condition: When a CONNECT packet does not conform to section 3.1
requirements.why_checkable: A nonconforming CONNECT can be followed by observation of connection closure.

requirements.quote: 2.The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT Packet conforms to section 3.1 and close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK if it does not conform [MQTT-3.1.4-1].
requirements.condition: When a CONNECT packet does not conform to section 3.1
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send CONNACK before closing the Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The outbound packet trace can verify absence of CONNACK before closure.

requirements.quote: 3.The Server MAY check that the contents of the CONNECT Packet meet any further restrictions and MAY perform authentication and authorization checks. If any of these checks fail, it SHOULD send an appropriate CONNACK response with a non-zero return code as described in section 3.2 and it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After basic CONNECT conformance validation
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to enforce further content restrictions.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes these additional restrictions optional and imposes no mandatory choice.

requirements.quote: 3.The Server MAY check that the contents of the CONNECT Packet meet any further restrictions and MAY perform authentication and authorization checks. If any of these checks fail, it SHOULD send an appropriate CONNACK response with a non-zero return code as described in section 3.2 and it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After basic CONNECT conformance validation
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to perform authentication checks.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes authentication optional in this statement and imposes no mandatory choice.

requirements.quote: 3.The Server MAY check that the contents of the CONNECT Packet meet any further restrictions and MAY perform authentication and authorization checks. If any of these checks fail, it SHOULD send an appropriate CONNACK response with a non-zero return code as described in section 3.2 and it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After basic CONNECT conformance validation
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to perform authorization checks.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes authorization optional in this statement and imposes no mandatory choice.

requirements.quote: 3.The Server MAY check that the contents of the CONNECT Packet meet any further restrictions and MAY perform authentication and authorization checks. requirements.quote:
If validation is successful the Server performs the following steps. 

1.If the ClientId represents a Client already connected to the Server then the Server MUST disconnect the existing Client [MQTT-3.1.4-2].

2.The Server MUST perform the processing of CleanSession that is described in section 3.1.2.4 [MQTT-3.1.4-3].

3.The Server MUST acknowledge the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK Packet containing a zero return code [MQTT-3.1.4-4].

4.Start message delivery and keep alive monitoring.
requirements.condition: After successful validation when the ClientId is already connected
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the existing Client before performing CleanSession processing.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process the new connection's CleanSession state before resolving the existing Client connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Event ordering in a duplicate-ClientId connection trace is directly observable.
